learn.hook: Your cotton T-shirt grew on a plant, your woollen sweater was once on a sheep, and your raincoat came from petroleum! Clothes have surprising beginnings.
points: Clothes are made of fabric, and fabric is made of thin threads called fibres.
Plant fibres: cotton comes from the fluffy balls (bolls) of the cotton plant, jute from the stem of the jute plant, and coir from coconut husks.
Animal fibres: wool comes from the hair of sheep, goats, yaks and camels. Silk comes from the cocoons made by silkworms.
Synthetic (man-made) fibres like nylon and polyester are made in factories from chemicals that come from petroleum.
Cotton soaks up sweat and is cool for summer. Wool traps air and keeps us warm in winter.

example.q: Think it through: why is cotton better than nylon for a hot summer day in Chennai?
steps: In hot weather we sweat a lot.
Cotton soaks up sweat and lets air pass through.
Nylon does not soak up sweat well, so we feel sticky.
example.answer: Cotton soaks up sweat and keeps us cool.

learn.reallife: Jute is called the 'golden fibre'. It is grown a lot in West Bengal and is used to make strong sacks, bags and ropes.

quiz.q: Cotton fibre comes from
options: the bolls of the cotton plant
the stem of the jute plant
quiz.explain: Cotton grows as soft fluffy fibre in the bolls (seed pods) of the cotton plant.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up cotton with other fibres

quiz.q: Which fibre comes from an animal?
quiz.explain: Silk comes from the cocoons spun by silkworms.
quiz.mistake: Thinks silk is made from a plant

quiz.q: Jute is often called the
quiz.explain: Jute fibres are shiny and golden-brown, so jute is called the golden fibre.
quiz.mistake: Does not know jute's nickname

quiz.q: What do silkworms eat?
quiz.explain: Silkworms feed on mulberry leaves before spinning their cocoons.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how silkworms are raised

quiz.q: Nylon and polyester are
quiz.explain: They are man-made fibres prepared from chemicals that come from petroleum.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all fibres come from plants or animals

quiz.q: Coir, used for doormats and ropes, comes from
quiz.explain: Coir is the rough fibre from the outer husk of coconuts. Kerala makes a lot of coir.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up coir with jute

quiz.q: Which fabric is best to keep you warm in a Shimla winter?
quiz.explain: Wool fibres trap air, and trapped air keeps body heat in.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any fabric keeps us equally warm

quiz.q: Pashmina wool comes from
quiz.explain: Pashmina comes from the soft under-hair of Changthangi goats that live in the cold of Ladakh.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the source of pashmina

teach.ask: Gappu fluffs his feathers: 'You have no feathers! What are your clothes made of? Where do the threads come from?'
teach.praise: Wow! Cotton and jute from plants, wool and silk from animals, and nylon from factories. Clothes have such stories!
teach.nudge: Which fibres come from plants? And which come from animals?

learn.hook: A cotton ball and a shirt look nothing alike. How does fluffy cotton become a smart school shirt? Let's follow the steps!
points: Cotton bolls are picked from the plants. Then the seeds are removed from the cotton. This is called ginning.
Fibres are twisted together to make a long thread called yarn. This is spinning. A charkha (spinning wheel) or a takli can spin yarn by hand.
Yarn is woven or knitted into fabric. Fabric is dyed or printed in colours, then cut and stitched into clothes.
For wool, sheep's hair is cut off (shearing, which does not hurt the sheep, like a haircut). It is washed, sorted, combed and spun into yarn.
For silk, silkworms spin cocoons. The fine silk thread is unwound from the cocoons and woven into silk fabric.

example.q: Mahatma Gandhi spun yarn on a charkha every day. Think it through: what is khadi?
steps: Gandhiji wanted Indians to make their own cloth.
Yarn was spun by hand on a charkha.
The yarn was then woven by hand into cloth.
example.answer: Khadi is cloth made from hand-spun and hand-woven yarn.

learn.reallife: If you visit a khadi shop, you'll see cloth made by hand-spinning and hand-weaving, just like in Gandhiji's time.

games.title: Cotton to shirt
games.prompt: Put the steps for making a cotton shirt in order

items.text: Removing seeds from cotton is called ___.
Cutting wool from a sheep is called ___.
Twisting fibres into yarn is called ___.
The spinning wheel used by Gandhiji is the ___.

quiz.q: What is ginning?
quiz.explain: In ginning, the cotton fibres are separated from the seeds.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up ginning with shearing

quiz.q: Making yarn by twisting fibres together is called
quiz.explain: Spinning twists short fibres into a long, strong thread called yarn.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up spinning and weaving

quiz.q: Which comes first in making a cotton shirt?
quiz.explain: First the cotton is picked; ginning, spinning, weaving, dyeing and stitching come later.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the order of steps

quiz.q: What is shearing?
options: Cutting the woolly hair off a sheep
quiz.explain: Shearing is like a haircut for sheep. It does not hurt them, and the wool grows back.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up shearing with ginning

quiz.q: After shearing, why is wool washed before spinning?
options: To remove dirt, dust and grease
quiz.explain: Raw wool has dirt and grease. Washing cleans it before it is combed and spun.
quiz.mistake: Does not know raw wool is dirty

quiz.q: Khadi is cloth that is
quiz.explain: Khadi is made from yarn spun by hand on a charkha and woven by hand.
quiz.mistake: Thinks khadi is a factory fabric

quiz.q: Silk thread is taken from the silkworm's
quiz.explain: Silkworms spin cocoons of fine silk thread, which is unwound to make silk.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where the silk thread is

quiz.q: Which tool can be used to spin yarn by hand?
quiz.explain: A takli is a small hand spindle used for spinning yarn. A charkha is a spinning wheel.
quiz.mistake: Does not know traditional spinning tools

teach.ask: Gappu holds some cotton fluff: 'How does this soft fluff turn into a shirt? Tell me the steps!'
teach.praise: Yay! Pick, gin, spin, weave, dye and stitch. Now I can make a shirt for my baby brother!
teach.nudge: What happens to the seeds? And how does fluff become a thread and then cloth?

learn.hook: Banarasi silk, Kanchipuram sarees, Pochampally ikat: India is famous around the world for its beautiful handmade textiles!
points: Weaving uses two sets of threads crossing each other at right angles on a loom. The long threads are the warp and the threads going across are the weft.
Knitting uses one long yarn made into loops. Sweaters and socks are often knitted.
A handloom is worked by hand and feet. A powerloom runs on electricity.
Famous textiles: Banarasi silk from Varanasi, Kanchipuram silk from Tamil Nadu, Pochampally ikat from Telangana, golden Muga silk from Assam, and Bandhani tie-dye from Gujarat and Rajasthan.
National Handloom Day is on 7 August. Old clothes can be reused as bags, mats or dusters, or given to someone who needs them.

example.q: Make a mini weave: cut paper strips (ask an adult to help with the scissors) and weave them through slits in a sheet of paper. Think it through: how do the strips go?
steps: Fix strips lengthwise: these are like the warp.
Push a new strip across, going over one and under the next: this is the weft.
The next strip starts the other way, under then over.
example.answer: Over-under strips crossing at right angles make a woven pattern, just like on a loom.

learn.reallife: Look at a cotton dupatta or a jute bag closely: you can see tiny threads going up-down and side-to-side. That is weaving!

games.title: Weave or knit?
items: Weaving uses two sets of threads.
The warp and the weft cross each other.
Knitting uses one long yarn made into loops.
That is why a knitted sweater can come apart from one pulled thread.
A powerloom is worked only by hand.
A powerloom runs on electricity; a handloom is worked by hand.
Warp and weft threads cross at right angles.
National Handloom Day is on 7 August.
India celebrates National Handloom Day on 7 August.
Bandhani is a kind of tie-dye.
Small bits of cloth are tied tightly before dyeing to make dotted patterns.

quiz.q: In weaving, at what angle do the warp and weft threads cross?
quiz.explain: Warp and weft cross at right angles, which is 90°.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that 'right angle' means 90°

quiz.q: The machine on which fabric is woven is called a
quiz.explain: Fabric is woven on a loom. A charkha and a takli are for spinning yarn.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up weaving tools with spinning tools

quiz.q: Sweaters and socks are usually made by
quiz.explain: Knitting makes loops from a single yarn, which gives stretchy fabric for sweaters and socks.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up knitting with weaving

quiz.q: Banarasi silk sarees are made in
quiz.explain: Banaras is another name for Varanasi, so its silk is called Banarasi silk.
quiz.mistake: Does not link Banaras with Varanasi

quiz.q: Golden Muga silk comes from
quiz.explain: Muga silk, with its natural golden shine, is made in Assam.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Muga silk with other silks

quiz.q: Bandhani is made by
options: painting with a brush on paper
tying small bits of cloth tightly and then dyeing it
quiz.explain: The tied parts don't take colour, so they make dotted patterns.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how tie-dye works

quiz.q: When is National Handloom Day celebrated?
quiz.explain: India celebrates National Handloom Day on 7 August to honour handloom weavers.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up national days

quiz.q: What is a good way to use old clothes that no longer fit?
options: Give them to someone who needs them or make bags and dusters
quiz.explain: Reusing and donating clothes reduces waste and helps others.
quiz.mistake: Thinks old clothes are just rubbish

teach.ask: Gappu tugs a thread from a mat: 'How are threads joined to make cloth? Is weaving the same as knitting?'
teach.praise: Now I know! Weaving crosses two sets of threads on a loom; knitting makes loops with one yarn. I can weave a nest better now!
teach.nudge: How do the threads go in weaving? And how is knitting different?
